standard_prerequisites.name: The inertia group is normal in the decomposition group, and the decomposition group acts on the residue field by the map to its automorphism group
standard_prerequisites.use: Explains why the formula of the statement is meaningful and what the action on the right hand side is.

standard_prerequisites.name: An inertia element acts on a uniformizer by multiplication by a unit, whose image in the residue field is the value of the inertia character
standard_prerequisites.use: Recalls the construction of the character, which the computation uses.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relation between the unit attached to an element of the decomposition group and the unit attached to its inverse, together with the triviality of inertia elements modulo the uniformizer
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the substitutions that turn the value at the conjugate into the conjugate of the value at the original element.

core_obligations: Recall the construction of the inertia character: choose a uniformizer of the local ring, write the translate of the uniformizer by an inertia element as a unit times the uniformizer, and take the image of that unit in the residue field (proof lines 33447-33453).

Record the auxiliary fact that for an element of the decomposition group the same writing is possible, and that the unit attached to the inverse is the inverse translate of the unit attached to the element (proof lines 33453-33457).

Compute the unit attached to the conjugate of an inertia element by the decomposition group, using the substitutions of the previous step and the multiplicativity of the action (proof lines 33457-33466).

Use that an inertia element acts trivially modulo the uniformizer to reduce the expression to the translate of the unit attached to the original inertia element, which is exactly the equivariance formula of the statement (proof lines 33466-33468).
proof_roadmap: Recall the definition of the inertia character through the ratios attached to a uniformizer (proof lines 33447-33453).
Write the auxiliary ratios for elements of the decomposition group and for inverses (proof lines 33453-33457).
Compute the ratio for a conjugate and reduce modulo the uniformizer to obtain the equivariance formula (proof lines 33457-33468).
difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that the inertia character of an extension of discretely valued fields is equivariant for the action of the decomposition group on the residue field, in the form that the value at a conjugate is the translate of the value at the original element (statement lines 33430-33439). The proof recalls the construction of the character as the residue class of the ratio between the translate of a uniformizer and the uniformizer itself, records the analogous ratios for elements of the decomposition group and for inverses, and then performs a displayed computation for the conjugate in which the triviality of inertia elements modulo the uniformizer reduces the expression to the translate of the original ratio (proof lines 33441-33468). The two substitutions at the start of the computation are what make the equivariance visible. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.
